label: a6-126-ex-cocountable-closure-detected-by-a-net-not-a-sequence
tail:
After a thorough adversarial review of the item and every quoted dependency, I find no fatal defects. The proof correctly shows that 2 belongs to the closure of \([0,1]\) in the cocountable topology (every neighbourhood of 2 has at most countable complement, so it meets the uncountable set \([0,1]\)), and it then applies `thm-closure-characterised-by-nets` to obtain a net in \([0,1]\) converging to 2. The argument that no sequence in \([0,1]\) converges to 2 is sound: the range of any such sequence is at most countable and excludes 2, so its complement is an open neighbourhood of 2 containing no sequence terms, violating the eventual‑in‑every‑neighbourhood condition from the definition of convergence. All citations match the dependency statements provided; no claim is false and no step depends on a missing hypothesis that a competent reader could not close within seconds.

0 fatal, 0 nonfatal
